procurement.title:
Technical components.
Selected for your application.
procurement.intro: Find the right technical component for your application. We connect component selection, technical advice and sourcing around your requirements.
lines: Component selection — Match function, interfaces and specifications.
Technical advice — Compare standard parts and suitable alternatives.
Sourcing — Align quantities, availability and documentation.

engineered.title:
Custom solutions.
Developed for your application.
engineered.intro: Start with the application, a drawing or a sample. We bring engineering, suitable sources and agreed checks together for your custom component.
lines: Application review — Define function, interfaces and operating conditions.
Custom development — Adapt standard parts or develop a custom solution.
Samples and checks — Agree evaluation criteria before release.

supplyChain.title:
Component supply.
Planned around your needs.
supplyChain.intro: Turn component demand into a coordinated supply plan. We align sourcing, stock arrangements and deliveries with your operational requirements.
lines: Supply planning — Align demand, order cycles and lead times.
Stock arrangements — Define inventory levels and replenishment terms.
Delivery coordination — Plan quantities, schedules and documentation.

series.title:
Series supply.
Built around your demand.
series.intro: Move from approved samples to repeat orders. We coordinate agreed specifications, recurring quantities and supply terms as your production needs develop.
lines: Release requirements — Agree specifications, samples and checks.
Repeat orders — Maintain agreed references and documentation.
Ongoing supply — Plan recurring deliveries and stock terms.

custom-solutions.title: From application to the right component
custom-solutions.intro: Function, interfaces and operating conditions define the task. We assess standard components, adaptations and custom parts, then coordinate the technical work and suitable sources.

partners.title: The right source for each requirement
partners.intro: Select sources by component, process and the evidence the application needs. Define responsibilities before the work begins.

inquiry.title: Start with what you have
inquiry.intro: A part number, drawing, sample or application description is a useful starting point. We clarify missing details and agree the next step before defining the offer.
bullets: Describe the required function and installation conditions.
Include quantities, existing documentation and preferred delivery dates.
Specify any checks, approvals or supply arrangements that matter.

process.title: From inquiry to agreed supply
process.intro: The scope determines the steps. Standard purchases and repeat orders can use existing specifications; samples and qualification are added where required.

steps.title: Share your requirement
steps.text: Send a part number, drawing, sample or description, with quantities and preferred dates.

steps.title: Clarify the application
steps.text: Clarify function, interfaces, operating conditions and the documentation needed.

steps.title: Select the approach
steps.text: Compare standard components, custom solutions and suitable sourcing or manufacturing routes.

steps.title: Agree the offer
steps.text: Confirm goods or project scope, price, responsibilities and delivery terms before proceeding.

steps.title: Check and approve
steps.text: Where needed, assess samples against agreed criteria and record the approval decision.

steps.title: Arrange supply
steps.text: Plan delivery and, if required, recurring orders, call-offs and stock terms.

technical-questions.title: Typical component requirements
technical-questions.intro: Component needs range from selecting an existing product to adapting a design or planning recurring supply. Start with the requirement that matches your application.

cards.title: Select a suitable component
cards.text: Compare the function, interfaces and operating conditions with the available product information. Clarify variants and manufacturer questions.

cards.title: Adapt an existing part
cards.text: A geometry, connector or interface needs to change. Define the differences, samples and qualification required for the application.

cards.title: Assess a replacement
cards.text: A component has changed or been discontinued. Compare requirements, technical differences and any renewed approval needed for the replacement.

cards.title: Plan a second source
cards.text: Assess an additional source against technical requirements and shared dependencies. Document differences and conditions for switching.

quality.title: Agreed requirements. Documented decisions.
quality.intro: Agree the checks, documentation and release responsibilities for the component and its intended use.

cards.title: Defined requirements
cards.text: Specify the function, interfaces, operating conditions and documentation used to assess the component.

cards.title: Samples & agreed checks
cards.text: Define which samples and checks are needed, including scope, responsibilities and criteria for assessment.

cards.title: Documented approval
cards.text: Record checked features, differences and the approval status for the agreed component version and application.

component-fields.title: Explore component fields
component-fields.intro: Compare the functions, interfaces and installation details that guide component selection.

heritage.title: Technical trade experience, rooted in WTS
heritage.intro: The Komponia offering builds on the technical component experience of WTS since 1997. It brings component selection, individual solutions and ongoing supply together for manufacturers and industrial users.

recurring-supply.title: Production-scale pricing. Deliveries that fit.
recurring-supply.intro: Produce in economical quantities and take delivery in smaller call-offs. We connect larger production lots with agreed safety stock, demand planning and recurring deliveries. Setup costs are spread across more parts, while release quantities follow your production schedule.

supply-terms.title: Clear terms for recurring supply
supply-terms.intro: Compare the complete supply cost: parts, packaging, freight and stock. Agree quantities, call-offs, stock ownership and change handling so that larger production lots remain aligned with your actual demand.

topics.title: Demand & quantities
topics.text: Plan economical production lots against expected consumption and the agreed planning period.

topics.title: Call-offs & delivery
topics.text: Match release quantities, packing and delivery frequency to your production needs.

topics.title: Stock terms
topics.text: Agree ownership, financing, acceptance and handling of unused stock.

topics.title: Changes & alternatives
topics.text: Define how product changes, ageing and alternative sources are assessed.

closing-cta.title: Have a component requirement in mind?
closing-cta.intro: Start with a part number, drawing or application description.

why-komponia.title: Technical expertise. Competitive prices.
why-komponia.intro: OEM support and competitive pricing belong together. We combine purchasing power, efficient production quantities and smarter shipping to reduce the cost of your component supply.

cards.title: Shared purchasing power.
cards.text: We bring together orders for different components across customers. The combined business with our manufacturing partners creates scope for better purchasing terms, including custom parts.

cards.title: Larger runs. Smaller call-offs.
cards.text: Agreed safety stock lets us plan larger production batches and spread setup costs across more parts. You call off smaller quantities to match your production needs.

cards.title: Smarter packing. Lower freight costs.
cards.text: Our AI-designed packing and shipping process considers dimensions, protection and delivery quantities together. Less empty space and coordinated shipments help lower freight cost per component.

environment.title: Less empty space. More considered resource use.
environment.intro: Environmental protection is part of how we plan supply. We work to reduce unnecessary packaging and transport volume, consolidate compatible deliveries and keep stock aligned with actual demand.
bullets: Size packaging around the parts and the protection they need.
Use available transport space more efficiently through coordinated shipments.
Review stock to limit unused parts and avoidable urgent deliveries.
